name: Hip hinge
equipment: a dowel or broom handle along the spine, optional
movement: standing, the hips pushed back and the trunk tipped forward with a flat back and soft knees, and back up

phone.placement: Stand the phone up on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to you.

words.hint: Standing: hips pushed back, trunk tipped forward with a flat back and soft knees, and back up.
words.start: Stand the phone up on the floor. Stand tall side on to it, feet hip-width apart, hands on your hips.
words.position: Stand tall side on to the phone, feet hip-width apart, knees soft, hands on the hips or a dowel held along the spine touching the head, upper back and tailbone.
words.top: The trunk tipped forward about halfway — forty to seventy five degrees — with the back long and the head in line, the hips pushed back, the knees soft and the shins upright.
howto: Stand tall, feet hip-width, knees soft, weight through the whole foot.
Push the hips straight back — as if closing a drawer with your bottom — and let the trunk tip forward. The back stays long, the head in line; the shins stay upright.
Go about halfway down — stop where the backs of the thighs pull or the back would round — and hold for the count.
Drive the hips forward to stand tall again, finishing with the glutes, not by leaning back. The rep counts there.
words.cannot: The lower back rounding a little under a flat-looking trunk: it sees the trunk angle, the knees, the shins and the head dropping. A dowel along the spine tells you what it cannot.
words.about: Hip hinge — standing side on: the hinge, as the hip-to-shoulder line off vertical, 40–75° at the bottom; a rep is under way past 25 and counts when the trunk is back under 12; the knees soft, 150–172° during the rep — more bend is a squat; the back long, the head and upper back within 20° of the line they had standing and not craning up more than 15°; the shins upright, no more than 105° from the floor; and no leaning back past upright between reps. Hold two seconds at the bottom. The pattern behind lifting safely, and the first thing a physio reteaches a back that hurts bending.
words.lost: Stand side on to the camera, the whole body in
words.early: Hold it at the bottom next time
words.safety: Only as far as the back stays flat. If the back rounds or the hamstrings pull hard, stop higher.
words.easier: A smaller hinge; hands on the hips; a shorter hold.
words.harder: A longer hold; a slower return; a light weight held at the shins.
words.mistakes: Squatting — bending the knees instead of pushing the hips back; rounding the back; looking up or letting the head drop; the shins tipping forward; leaning back to finish.

measurements.label: trunk tipped forward
measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off vertical, + forward: 0 upright, 90 flat. Also the progress measurement.

settings.label: Trunk tipped at the bottom, at least (degrees from upright)
Trunk tipped at the bottom, at most

measurements.label: standing tall

settings.label: Leaning back standing, at most (degrees, negative)

measurements.why: The trunk off plumb while standing between reps, + forward: finishing the rep by leaning back past upright, instead of standing tall on the glutes, reads below 0.

measurements.label: knees soft
measurements.why: The knee: 180 locked, under 150 a squat. Soft is 15–25° of bend.

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (less is a squat)
Knee angle, at most (180 is locked)

measurements.label: back long
measurements.why: How far the shoulder sits off the line from the ear to the hip, as its change since standing: + the head and upper back dropping (the back rounding), − the head craning up. The lower back under a flat-looking trunk is not seen.

settings.label: Head lifted off the back's line, at most (degrees, negative)
Head and upper back dropped, at most (degrees from the start)

measurements.label: shin from the floor
measurements.why: The ankle-to-knee line from the floor: 90 is the shin upright, more the knee travelling forward over the toes — a squat, not a hinge.

settings.label: Shin from the floor, at most (90 is upright)

faults.label: Leaning back
faults.text: Stand tall — finish with the glutes, don’t lean back

faults.label: Hinge short
faults.text: Hinge a little further — hips back

faults.label: Too far
faults.text: Not so far — about halfway down is enough

faults.label: Squatting
faults.text: Don’t squat — hips back, knees only soft
faults.deep: The knees are bending too much — push the hips straight back

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.text: Keep the back long — chest and head in line
faults.deep: The back is rounding — come up to where it stays long

faults.label: Looking up
faults.text: Don’t look up — keep the back of the head long

faults.label: Shins tipping
faults.text: Shins upright — push the hips back
faults.deep: The knees are travelling forward — push the hips back instead

settings.label: Trunk angle that counts as under way
